themes.consensus_view: Most desks now treat the AI buildout as a credit and cash-flow story rather than a pure growth story, with bond markets balking at hyperscaler debt and the bull case hinging on AI revenue picking up before spending peaks.

facts_agreed.claim: The AI infrastructure buildout has become a financing/credit story that is straining bond markets, not just an equity trade.
evidence_quotes: AI is increasingly becoming a credit story rather than just an equity story.
The private sector is now visibly competing with the public sector for the same waning duration bid
hyperscaler spreads widening, CDS blowing out, deal concessions expanding

facts_agreed.claim: The market is no longer willing to reward hyperscaler capex ambition on faith and is now demanding proof of cash-flow returns.
evidence_quotes: the market is no longer willing to treat spend as costless
markets don't run on long-term visions. They run on cash flow.

facts_contested.claim: Whether AI capex spending keeps rising or is due for a slowdown
facts_contested.for_evidence: there is no plateau in AI capex
facts_contested.against_evidence: the case that this narrative experiences a serious “hiccup” is growing.

themes.consensus_view: Eight desks reference the Middle East and US-Iran conflict as a live risk to oil and supply chains, but none has committed to a clear directional call on whether it escalates or calms.

facts_agreed.claim: Banks across eight desks flag Middle East and US-Iran conflict escalation as a live macro catalyst this window, without staking a directional view.

themes.consensus_view: The research leans toward a live risk that the Fed raises rates at its July meeting rather than holding, with market-implied hike odds jumping to roughly 35-40% and at least one bank arguing current rates are too low to bring inflation down, though most desks only flag the meeting as a key date to watch without staking a call.

facts_agreed.claim: A Fed rate hike is a real and possibly underappreciated risk, with current policy seen by some as not restrictive enough to tame inflation.
evidence_quotes: Markets may be underpricing a July Fed hike
the Fed’s policy rate has been too low and thus not restrictive enough

themes.consensus_view: Five banks reference tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea as a live supply and oil-price risk, but none has staked out a clear directional call on how it resolves.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks flag tanker traffic disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea as an active supply-chain and oil-market catalyst this window.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic disruption
Strait of Hormuz fertilizer supply chain disruption
US-Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz navigation

themes.consensus_view: Three desks see money quietly moving into defensive corners of the market — low-volatility names, healthcare, telecom, and biopharma — as high-flying tech loses steam, and none of them pushes back.

facts_agreed.claim: A defensive rotation is underway beneath the market surface as investors shift out of high-beta tech into safer pockets.
evidence_quotes: starting to see a more defensive trade below the surface
more defensive rotation exiting the week
historical precedents show these types of generalist-driven non-fundamental rotations into biopharma can linger

themes.consensus_view: Banks across four desks flag the Iran and Middle East conflict as a live threat to oil supply that is pushing crude prices higher, though only one has framed it as an outright bullish oil call.

facts_agreed.claim: The Iran and broader Middle East conflict is threatening oil supply through key shipping chokepoints and pushing crude prices higher.

themes.consensus_view: Banks agree that US government bond yields are climbing and the yield curve is steepening, but only Bloomberg reads it as a warning that inflation is about to become a real problem while the others just flag the move without a directional call.

facts_agreed.claim: US and global government bond yields are rising and the yield curve is steepening.
The steepening real yield curve is read as a market signal that inflation is set to become troublesome.
evidence_quotes: this is the market’s way of saying inflation is going to become troublesome

themes.consensus_view: Several bank desks flag new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Congressional testimony and policy stance as a live macro watch-item, but none has yet staked out a directional view on what it means for rates.

facts_agreed.claim: Three research desks reference Fed Chair Warsh's Congressional testimony and monetary-policy approach as a topic to watch this window.
